title: HTTP & REST Basics
intro: HTTP and REST interview questions appear in every Python backend fresher screen because APIs are what backend developers build. This page covers the HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE — and the idempotency distinction the interviewer always probes), the status code groups that matter for a backend developer (2xx success, 3xx redirect, 4xx client error, 5xx server error — with the 200 vs 201 vs 204, 400 vs 401 vs 403 vs 404 comparisons that come up constantly), the request-response cycle (client sends request → server processes → server sends response — what travels in the header vs the body), JSON as the dominant API data format (how to parse it in Python with json.loads and json.dumps), the REST constraints (stateless, resource-based URLs, uniform interface — at the concept level), token-based authentication basics (why we send a token in the header, not a password), and the Python requests library for calling APIs from code.
